title: Best RFI Software in 2026: A Buyer's Guide for Sales and Proposal Teams
summary: Compare 7 RFI software on AI accuracy, pricing, and team fit with real user reviews and a built-in evaluation framework.
body_markdown:
Most RFI responses don't lose deals because the product is wrong. They lose because teams still write responses manually, tracking down answers, digging through old documents, and reformatting 200-row spreadsheets against a deadline, and that produces responses that are slow, inconsistent, or contradict an earlier bid.


The right[RFI software](https://www.inventive.ai/solution/ai-rfi-response-software) fixes this. It connects to your knowledge base, attributes every answer to a verified source, and catches conflicting information before it reaches an evaluator. This guide covers the 7 best tools in 2026 and how to evaluate them before you commit.


Most RFI response tools are built around a content library: the AI responds to incoming questions to pre-approved answers. If a buyer asks something outside that library, the platform can't help and manual writing takes over.


## **TL;DR**


- **Inventive AI:** A fully autonomous AI agent platform that automates the entire RFI response, delivering 2x higher-quality answers, built-in conflict detection, zero hallucinations, active content governance, and an easy-to-use interface for every contributor.
- **Loopio:** If your team already runs on an established content library, Loopio's section-based assignment and freshness indicators keep it organized and reviewable. What it won't do is answer outside that library or catch two entries that contradict each other.
- **Responsive:** Complex approval chains are where Responsive earns its keep, with multi-gate workflows and a Trust Score attached to every answer. That score tells you how closely a response matches stored content, not whether the content itself is still correct.
- **SiftHub:** Because it pulls live CRM and deal context into every response, SiftHub works best when an RFI is tied to an active deal. The tradeoff is that response quality rises and falls with how clean that CRM data is.
- **AutoRFP:** For teams handling repetitive, high-volume RFIs, AutoRFP reuses proven language quickly and reliably. Ask it something more technical or buyer-specific, and the answers can start to feel generic.
- **Arphie:** Every answer comes with its source and reasoning attached, so reviewers can see exactly why the AI landed where it did, which matters for compliance-heavy RFIs. It stops short of flagging conflicts between source documents.
- **Qvidian:** Living inside Word with a centralized library and a full audit trail, Qvidian fits regulated enterprises already on Upland. Its output is only as current as the library behind it.

## **2. Loopio**


[Loopio](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/loopio-pricing-features-reviews) is one of the legacy platforms in the RFI response market. It uses a structured answer library with an auto-fill feature that respond to incoming RFI questions to pre-approved content.


For RFI teams specifically, it supports section-based assignment so different contributors can own different parts of the questionnaire simultaneously. Freshness indicators flag answers that haven't been reviewed recently, giving reviewers a way to prioritize verification before submission.


### **Limitations**


When buyers ask questions outside the stored library, the platform doesn't generate answers from broader documentation, manual writing takes over. There's no conflict detection across stored answers.


### **Pricing**


Contact for pricing. Foundations, Enhanced, and Enterprise tiers.


### **Customer Review**


A verified[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/loopio/reviews) reviewer said Loopio works well for cross-functional collaboration on RFPs. But they also said the interface is "clunky and non-intuitive," with a narrow range of view options and limited export formats.


### **Who it's best for**


RFI teams that respond to similar questionnaires at volume and have the capacity to maintain a content library.

## **3. Responsive (formerly RFPIO)**


[Responsive](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/responsive-ai-rfpio-pricing-features-reviews) has been in the response management market for nearly a decade as a legacy platform. For RFI teams, it assigns a Trust Score (0–100) to every AI-generated answer based on library match strength, on a long questionnaire, that signal helps reviewers focus on lower-confidence responses rather than checking everything equally.


Multi-gate approval routing, SME assignment by section, and a pre-export quality check that flags missing responses and sensitive data are all built into the platform. It integrates with Salesforce, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.


### **Limitations**


The Trust Score measures how closely an AI-generated answer respond to what's stored in the library, not whether that stored content is still accurate. An answer written 18 months ago can score 95/100 if it matches the library entry, even if the underlying information has since changed. There's no automated flag for stale content, so the review burden still sits with the Proposal Manager. Before moving to any decision, you can check out Responsive[alternatives](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfpio-competitors-alternatives) for a detailed platform comparison.


### **Pricing**


Lite edition starts at $5,000/year for 5 users. Emerging, Growth, and Enterprise tiers available through the sales team.


### **Customer Review**


A verified[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews) reviewer said Responsive helps standardize and improve their tender process. But they also said the CSM (customer success manager) experience was only "good, not great."


### **Who it's best for**


Large enterprise teams managing RFIs with multi-departmental approval requirements and an existing Salesforce setup.

## **4. SiftHub**


[SiftHub](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/sifthub-pricing-features-reviews) is a presales enablement platform that pulls CRM data into the RFI response process. When an RFI comes in, the platform surfaces deal context like buyer details, deal stage, prior interactions, alongside the team's documentation to generate answers. It handles RFI intake across Word, Excel, and procurement portals via browser extension, and tracks contributor assignments so Proposal Managers can monitor progress without manual follow-ups.


### **Limitations**


SiftHub is built primarily for presales workflows, which means its RFI capabilities are tied to how well your CRM data is structured and maintained. If deal data is incomplete or inconsistently updated, the buyer-specific context it generates will reflect those gaps. Response quality still depends on what's stored in the team's documentation, with no conflict detection when sources disagree. The platform is relatively new, with limited independent review data with 1 Gartner review which makes it harder to assess how it performs at scale or across complex, multi-section RFIs. .

But they also said it sometimes answers a technical question from a functional angle, or the reverse, when the wording is similar, and flagged formatting issues on exported Excel files with complex tables.


### **Who it's best for**

## **5. AutoRFP**


[AutoRFP](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/autorfp-ai-pricing-features-reviews) generates first draft responses from a content library built from past approved submissions and uploaded documents. It accepts RFIs in Word, Excel, PDF, and web portal formats, and exports the completed response back in the buyer's original file.


Each answer is assigned a Trust Score that signals how closely the AI's source material matched the requirement, a useful signal for reviewers working through a long questionnaire.


### **Limitations**


AutoRFP works best on repetitive, reusable RFIs. On technically complex or buyer-specific questions, answers tend to run generic. Compliance tagging is automated but surface level, it confirms a response was provided, not whether it actually answers what was asked.


The interface is a real friction point.[G2 reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/autorfp-ai/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) call it janky and hard to use, and reorganizing a questionnaire mid-review slows you down when you've got fifty answers to get through before a deadline. ## **How to Evaluate RFI Response Software Before You Book a Demo**


‍


Most RFI software looks impressive in a demo. The real question is how it performs on your files, your questions, and your team's actual workflow, and that takes more than a vendor walkthrough to find out.


### **Map your biggest time sink first**


Before you look at a single tool, spend 20 minutes auditing where your team actually loses time in an RFI cycle. Is it the first draft? Chasing SMEs for answers? Review cycles? Reformatting the final file? The tool that solves your real bottleneck will deliver more value than the one with the longest feature list. Write down the top two time sinks before your first demo, and use those as the filter for every conversation.


### **Define a success metric before the pilot**


Most teams go into a trial without a clear benchmark. Decide upfront what success looks like: is it hours saved per RFI? First-draft approval rate? Turnaround time? Pick one metric, measure where you are today, and evaluate every tool against that number during the trial. It makes the final decision objective rather than impressionistic.


### **Run the pilot on a past RFI**


Pick an RFI you submitted in the last 60 days, one where you know exactly what the right answer looks like. Run the tool against it, then sit your submitted response next to the AI draft and score it question by question. Where does the AI nail it? Where does it go generic or pull the wrong source? Those gaps tell you more about real-world accuracy than any vendor demo ever will, because vendors always run demos on clean, pre-loaded data that's nothing like your actual knowledge base.


### **Evaluate reviewer effort separately**


The draft is only half the product. Count how many clicks and screens it takes one reviewer to check, comment on, and approve 50 answers. A tool that generates a strong first draft but buries the review workflow in a clunky interface will cost your team more time than it saves. Pay attention to how fast an experienced reviewer can move through the queue.


### **Dig into integration depth**


A tool that "integrates with Salesforce" could mean anything from pulling a contact name to syncing full account history. During the demo, ask the vendor to show you exactly what data flows in, how frequently it syncs, and whether it requires a manual trigger. The integrations that matter are the ones that remove a step your team currently does by hand.


### **Ask for the onboarding-to-value timeline**


Some tools go live in 48 hours; others take three months to reach full coverage. Ask the vendor specifically: at what point in onboarding do teams typically see their first meaningful time saving? What does the library need to contain before the AI draft quality becomes usable? That answer tells you how long you're committing to a ramp period before the tool actually pays off.

## **FAQs**


**Can the same tool handle RFIs, RFPs, and**[DDQs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/how-to-respond-to-a-ddq) **or do I need separate software?**


Most platforms in this list handle all three. The workflow is similar across formats, import, generate, review, export. The difference is depth: some tools treat RFIs as secondary to RFPs. Before buying, run a sample from each format you actually respond to. Don't rely on the format the vendor demos first.


**How long does implementation take before the tool is actually useful?** Library-based tools like Loopio and Responsive require you to build and populate a content library before the AI generates useful drafts, that process typically takes 4–12 weeks. AI-native platforms that connect directly to your documentation are generating drafts within days because there's no library to build first.


**What happens to my content library if I switch tools?** Most platforms export stored Q&A pairs as CSV or Excel, but the formatting rarely transfers cleanly. Plan for a manual cleanup phase. If you're switching to a platform that reads live documentation directly, the migration is simpler, your documentation is already where it needs to be.


**Does AI-generated RFI content create any legal or compliance risk?** Two areas to check: data privacy and content accuracy. Confirm the vendor doesn't use your content to train its AI, and verify data residency meets your requirements. On accuracy, AI answers referencing outdated certifications or incorrect product details create downstream liability, which is why source attribution and conflict detection matter before responses reach the buyer.


**How do I calculate**[ROI](https://www.inventive.ai/roi-calculator) **on RFI response software?**


Take your average hours per RFI, multiply by monthly RFI volume, and apply your team's hourly cost. That's your baseline. After 60 days on the new tool, measure the same numbers. Also track first-draft acceptance rate, how much the AI output changes before submission. Win rate on RFI-attached deals is harder to attribute cleanly, but it's the number that justifies the budget.


**Can RFI software submit directly into procurement portals like SAP Ariba?** Some can do via browser extension. Inventive AI or AutoRFP both support direct portal submission, the extension populates form fields rather than requiring copy-paste. Not every platform supports every portal, so confirm compatibility with the specific systems your buyers use before starting a trial.


**How do I get internal SMEs to actually use the review workflow?** The platforms with the highest SME participation are the ones where reviewing is fast. If a contributor has to navigate multiple screens to approve a straightforward answer, they disengage quickly. During your pilot, time how long it takes a first-time SME to review and approve 10 answers with zero training. That number predicts adoption better than any feature walkthrough.
